podcast.title: Supported Donald Trump
podcast.body: Ace Frehley was listed as one of the musicians who showed support for Donald Trump, making him an exception among many artists who declined to perform. "Outside of Kid Rock, Ted Nugent, three doors down and ace freely."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Supportive Crew
podcast.body: The crew working for Ace Frehley during his US tour with The Trews were noted for being "super accommodating and really sweet." This support was particularly appreciated by Colin McDonald, who was suffering from a severe bronchial infection at the time. "their crew was always really cool with us. They were super accommodating and really sweet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

podcast.title: US Tour with The Trews
podcast.body: Ace Frehley toured the United States with The Trews as his opening act for a six-week trek, performing in House of Blues venues across the country. The audiences for these shows were predominantly "die-hard Kiss fans" who were not necessarily open to new music. "We ended up doing like six week trek, opening for Ace Freyly at House of Blues all over America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

xref.title: Colin McDonald's Illness on Ace Frehley Tour
xref.body: Before a six-week US tour opening for Ace Frehley at House of Blues venues, Colin McDonald contracted a severe bronchial infection, losing his singing voice for the first three weeks. The audience, largely "die hard Kiss fans," were not typically receptive to new music. He eventually recovered his voice after obtaining antibiotics in America, leading Ace Frehley's famous sound engineer, Nightbob, to jokingly comment that he was "learning how to sing on this tour." "for the first like three weeks at Ace Freyly tour, I couldn't sing. It was a nightmare."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Trews: In Their Own Words

xref.title: Illness on Ace Frehley Tour
xref.body: Colin McDonald suffered a severe bronchial infection before and during the first three weeks of a six-week US tour opening for Ace Frehley. This left him unable to sing his usual high, hard vocal parts, which was particularly challenging given the audience was primarily "die-hard Kiss fans." He eventually recovered his voice after getting antibiotics in the US. "for the first like three weeks at Ace Freyly tour, I couldn't sing. It was a nightmare."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Running Crazed Management
xref.body: In addition to her label work, Marsha Zazula also operated Crazed Management. Her management roster included notable artists such as Ace Frehley of Kiss, Ministry, Testament, and King's X, demonstrating her significant role in artist development and career guidance. "She also ran crazed management, which included clients like Ace Freely of Kiss, Ministry, Testament, and King's X."
